The two sub-layers inside each Transformer encoder layer are a multi-head self-attention mechanism and a simple, position-wise fully connected feed-forward network.

MultiHead(Q, K, V) is computed by concatenating the attention heads and then projecting them with a parameter matrix $W^O$:

$$\text{MultiHead}(Q, K, V) = \text{Concat}(\text{head}_1, ..., \text{head}_h)W^O$$
$$\text{where } \text{head}_i = \text{Attention}(QW_i^Q, KW_i^K, VW_i^V)$$

where the projections are parameter matrices $W_i^Q \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}$, $W_i^K \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}$, $W_i^V \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_v}$, and $W^O \in \mathbb{R}^{h d_v \times d_{\text{model}}}$.

ColPali's late-interaction operator $LI(q, d)$ is computed as the sum over all query vectors of their maximum dot product with each of the document embedding vectors. Mathematically, it is expressed as:

$$LI(q, d) = \sum_{i=1}^{N_q} \max_{j=1}^{N_d} \langle \mathbf{E_q}^{(i)} | \mathbf{E_d}^{(j)} \rangle$$

where $\mathbf{E_q}$ and $\mathbf{E_d}$ represent the multi-vector embeddings of the query and document, respectively, and $\langle \cdot | \cdot \rangle$ represents the dot product.
